extracted.intended_audience: political theorists, constitutional designers, lawmakers, and students of republican government
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for designing stable republican/mixed constitutions (separation of powers, checks and balances, selection and accountability of magistrates, safeguards for minorities). Intended to assess features that promote liberty and prevent factional usurpation or civil disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent judiciary
rubrics_metrics.description: “The right Constitution of a right independent tribunal, to judge of controversies, is indispensable; and an upright, independent, judiciary tribunal, in a simple democracy, is impossible.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges must have security of tenure and independence from the momentary will of the majority (not mere durante bene placito). Without secure commissions and procedural protections (formal trial, full defence), courts become tools of the majority and will give no remedy to minorities. Mixed governments protect judicial independence because removal requires concurrence of multiple branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed government / balance of powers
rubrics_metrics.description: In a mixed government the judges cannot be displaced but by the concurrence of two branches... when there are three branches, after two have offered all possible arguments, and cannot agree, the third has only to consider which is nearest justice, and join with that, to decide the controversy and restore the peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a constitution with multiple independent branches (at least three) so that no single faction can control justice or remove checks; bicameralism and distinct executive, legislative, and judicial powers allow disputes to be resolved without civil war. Examples used: Roman and English mixtures; the three-branch balance helps preserve fixed rules for settling disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the 'utmost remedy' only for manifest fundamental attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: That the 'utmost remedy' is not to be used upon every distemper or default of those that shall be intrusted with the people's power and authority... such cautions are provided by the constitution itself, that civil dissensions can scarcely ever arise; or, if they do, may be easily composed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extreme remedies (violence, revolution, arms) should be reserved for clear, entrenched assaults on fundamentals of liberty. In systems lacking institutional redress (simple democracies), minorities may be driven to arms; properly mixed constitutions should provide legal channels for redress to avoid civil war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit-based selection of magistrates (avoid fashion/affection)
rubrics_metrics.description: That in all elections of magistrates, they have an especial eye upon the public, in making choice of such persons only as have appeared most eminent and active in the establishment and love of freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elect or appoint officials based principally on demonstrated public-minded service and merit rather than factional ties, patronage, or transient popularity. The text notes practical difficulties (people vote for friends), so institutional design (separation of powers, bicameral review, impeachment mechanisms) must supplement this ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not place unchecked trust in revolutionary or popular leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: “In the hands of those who have appeared most eminent and active in the establishment of freedom, may be safely placed the guardianship of liberty” — followed by a warning that such unlimited confidence has surrendered national liberties (example: Oliver Cromwell).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying solely on the patriotism or virtue of individuals; institutional constraints (term limits, recallability, divided powers, impeachment) are necessary because character and motives may change and leaders can betray liberties despite prior service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of laws over assumed popular virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the laws alone that really love the country... and that form of government which unites all the virtue, honour, and fear of the citizens, in a reverence and obedience to the laws, is the only one in which liberty can be secure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional design should make laws and institutions the principal guardians of the commonwealth rather than depending on citizens’ or leaders’ innate virtue, frugality, or love of equality; combine incentives (honour, fear, law) within structure to bind private interests to the public good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent concentration of authority (guard against tyranny of the majority)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most desperate, irremediable, and forlorn condition of liberty is in that very collection of all authority into one centre... the majority uncontrouled would not always behave discreetly and moderately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design distributed authority and institutional checks so that a dominant majority cannot unilaterally overturn rights or entrench itself. Historical examples (Rome, civil wars) show dangers when too much authority is centralized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elections: avoid being led by fashion, alliance, or affection
rubrics_metrics.description: That in all their elections... they be not led by any bent of fashion, alliance, or affection, and that none be taken in but purely on the account of merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electoral rules and cultural norms should discourage factional voting driven by clientelism, patronage, or fashionable influence. Because human behavior often thwarts this ideal, institutional remedies (multiple assemblies, checks) are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance accountability with protection from calumny
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid false charges, accusations, and calumninations, against persons in authority, which are the greatest abuses and blemishes of liberty... it is the secret of liberty, that all magistrates and public officers be kept in an accountable state... and that the people have freedom to accuse whom they please.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create mechanisms (independent grand juries, impartial tribunals, senate review) that let citizens hold officials accountable while deterring and punishing malicious false accusations (the Romans’ Turpitianum example). Safeguards must prevent accountability mechanisms from being weaponized by the dominant party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of appointment power and bicameral correction
rubrics_metrics.description: To separate the executive power from the legislature, make it responsible to one part of the legislature, on the impeachment of another, for the act of its power of appointment to offices, and to appoint two assemblies in the legislature, that the errors of one may be corrected by the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vest appointment power and removal/accountability across different institutions (e.g., executive appoints, one legislative chamber holds to account, the other confirms) and use bicameralism to correct mistakes and check factional capture of appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit continuations of power; guard against permanent trusts
rubrics_metrics.description: They should beware of ingratitude and unhandsome returns to such as have done eminent services for the commonwealth... not to impose a trust in the hands of any person or persons, further than as they may take it back again at pleasure. The reason is, honores mutant mores. Accessions and continuations of power expose the mind to temptations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid perpetual or indefinite grants of power or honors; retain mechanisms (term limits, revocation, recall, periodic reappointment) so that service does not calcify into entrenched privilege that corrupts character and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design institutions assuming self-interested passions, not universal virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue in a republic is not mere absence of ambition and avarice... one may venture to suspect that love of democracy, love of equality, and love of frugality are fanciful passions; nations act from passions and prejudices rather than constant self-sacrifice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame constitutional mechanisms on realistic assumptions about human nature (ambition, avarice, faction) rather than idealized universal virtue; use structure (checks, incentives, law) to align private passions with public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process in removal and impeachment
rubrics_metrics.description: This cannot be without a formal trial, and a full defence... in other [governments] a judge may be removed, or condemned to infamy, without any defence, or hearing, or trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that removal, impeachment, or condemnation of public officers follows formal, adversarial procedures guaranteeing full defense and fair trial to prevent arbitrary or party-driven purges, which otherwise make officials permanently insecure and courts tools of majorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pure/simple democracy; prefer constitutional mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: No democracy ever did or can exist... the word democracy signifies nothing more nor less than a nation or people without any government at all, and before any constitution is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject designs relying on pure direct democracy for large polities; instead adopt mixed or representative constitutional forms with institutional checks (separation of powers, bicameralism, judicial safeguards) to produce stability and protect minorities.
